Results.ReviewText:
Thoughts after about a month of use.
 - Overall satisfied with grilling performance. 
 - Heats up fast
 - The steaming rack could be deeper in depth.  It's barely wide enough to hold a typical 12"x10" aluminum tray of veggies.  I've managed to get one on, but at risk of having it fall over into the grilling area
 - I don't care for the open storage area.  Even with a cover, I can't keep tools in here because they fall out when you have to move the grill
 - Moving the grill is awkward.  No handles to lift the grill and roll it around.  I lift under the gas control knobs when having to move it on our patio.  Since it is stored up next to our house I have to pull it away for each use.  Having smaller wheels on the left legs would've helped a lot.

Results.ReviewText: It's a grill, it cooks by heat generated from propane. There are many less expensive grills that will cook from heat just fine. The big big difference is the build quality.  There is no denying that the Weber grills are well built.  Hopefully this grill will look good and be reliable for many years to come. My previous non-Weber grill lasted for many years (16) but I had to replace grills and burners multiple times during it's lifetime.

Results.OriginalProductName: Spirit II E-310 Gas Grill (Liquid Propane)
Results.ReviewText: Bought this as a new addition to our new home. We gave our last Weber grill (17years old) to my daughter and it's still performing like the first day we got it.  The new grill was easy to assemble. The instructions were easy to follow, no missing or damaged parts and all parts fit precisely together. This grill heats up fast and the cooking surface heat was uniformly even. We were able to 6 steaks without having to move them around. The construction seems to be just as durable as our old Weber. These grills may seem pricey to some people but if you take care of it, it will last longer than replacing cheaper grills 2 or 3 times.
Results.Title: Weber Quality

Results.ReviewText: After years of having grills that stopped working after just a few Summers of use, I decided to go with the weber largely because of the warranty. Overall im happy with it, easy to light and burns hot.  Though the burners do make noise like they aren't fully operating which is something I didn't want to deal with, espeically since I had it assembled by the store. Some portions of it feel cheap (like the wheel assembly which are cheap plastic) For what I paid, I expected a bit more design consideration. I'd love a grill maker that would put nice big off-road style wheels on their grill. If you're looking for a grill with a good warranty and is somewhat higher in quality, I'd spend a bit more. I realize this is sort of entry-level for weber and thats essentially what you get.
Results.Title: Just okay for the money
